title: cd2030.core
text: Countdown 2030 analysis routine health facility data. cd2030.core loads country’s facility data, checks quality, adjusts incomplete reporting outliers, chooses denominators, computes coverage, inequality, mortality, service utilization, health system family planning indicators, chart. also holds everything Countdown Shiny apps share: analysis pages, Load Data wizard, filters app frame (cd_app()), Countdown’s content report builder (standard reports, charts tables report can hold). used two ways: R, analysis library: load dataset, call functions, plot results. apps, cd2030.rmncah, cd2030.vaxx cd2030.pooled, Shiny front ends run inside DataSuite.

title: cd2030.core
text: datasuite.ui (https://github.com/damurka/datasuite.ui) generic layer: Shiny/React components, page frame, chart options Word/PowerPoint/PDF report engine. cd2030.core plugs Countdown (report content report_register(), translations cd_register_translations(), .onLoad). datasuite.ui never calls cd2030.core. apps (https://github.com/damurka/cd2030.rmncah, .vaxx, .pooled) set options, list pages call cd_app(). countdown-analytics (https://github.com/damurka/countdown-analytics) DataSuite extension. shinyApps entries name app’s package; DataSuite installs extension installed, updates extension updated, launches . Every package published https://damurka.r-universe.dev (built push main). Bayesian model uses bayescoveragemodel bayescoveragedeploy, suggested packages https://alkemalab.r-universe.dev.
code: DataSuite (VS Code based)   └─ countdown-analytics            the DataSuite extension: lists the apps, adds the AI tools        └─ cd2030.rmncah / cd2030.vaxx / cd2030.pooled    the apps, one R package each: run_app()             └─ cd2030.core          THIS PACKAGE: analysis, Countdown pages, wizard, report content                  └─ datasuite.ui    generic interface kit, chart options, report builder (knows nothing of Countdown)

Chart options reports. Every chart finished saved options (cd_finish_plot(), options datasuite.ui’s cd_chart_options(), re-exported ). report_presets() Countdown’s standard reports; export_report() (datasuite.ui, re-exported) writes report dataset.
code: library(cd2030.core)  # A dataset: the Countdown Excel workbook (Admin, Population, Reporting and service sheets), a Stata .dta master # file, or a saved .rds. The result is a CacheConnection: the data plus every choice made about it. path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core") cache <- load_cache_data(path) data <- cache$countdown_data      # the checked data (a cd_data tibble); load_data(path) gives just this  # Data quality calculate_average_reporting_rate(data) calculate_outliers_summary(data) calculate_overall_score(data, threshold = 90) plot(calculate_district_reporting_rate(data, threshold = 90))  # Adjustment, denominators and coverage go through the cache, which remembers each choice. Coverage also needs the # national rates and survey estimates the Load Data wizard collects (cache$set_national_estimates(), # cache$set_survey_estimates(), ...); the apps' pages show what each analysis needs. cache$set_k_factors(c(anc = 0.25, idelv = 0.25, vacc = 0.25, opd = 0.25))   # opd only for rmncah coverage <- cache$calculate_indicator_coverage("national")  # A standard report, written as Word (or "pdf", or "pptx" for a slide deck) reports <- report_presets("en") export_report(cache, reports[["data_quality"]], "data_quality.docx", format = "docx")  # Save the dataset and its choices next to the data, to reopen later with load_cache_data("kenya.rds") cache$set_cache_path("kenya.rds")

(?countdown-pages)     upload_ui = cd_upload_data_ui, upload_server = cd_upload_data_server   ) }

title: CacheConnection class — CacheConnection
text: R6 class handles persistent -memory caching data used Countdown 2030 analysis reporting workflows. Dependency Architecture: Layer 0 (Core Data): Raw countdown_data, thresholds, external surveys (un_estimates). Layer 1 (DQA & Adjustments): Depends Layer 0. Includes adjusted_data, reporting rates, completeness, overall scores. Layer 2 (Coverage & Denominators): Depends Layer 1. Includes derived coverages national, admin level 1, district levels. Layer 3 (Inequality & Health Systems): Depends Layer 2 (Coverage). Includes inequalities, mortality ratios, service utilization summaries.

"custom": Uses user-defined k_factors different indicator groups, values 0 1. "none": Returns data without adjustments. k_factors named numeric vector custom k-factor values 0 1 indicator group (e.g., c(anc = 0.3, idelv = 0.2, ...)). Used adjustment = "custom". settings adjustment settings (adjustment_settings_default(); Data Adjustment page's): years areas removed, indicator's k, outlier missing-value switches, everywhere area. given, adjustment k_factors used. steps TRUE: list data step (completeness, outliers, missing), showing changed (see generate_adjustment_values()).

title: Adjust service data for coverage analysis — adjust_service_data
text: cd_adjusted_data object containing adjusted service data, outliers flagged managed, missing values imputed.

title: Adjust service data for coverage analysis — adjust_service_data
text: Prepares service data series steps ensure data quality consistency: Validation: Checks structure .data ensures adjustment argument valid. custom adjustments, k_factors must specified contain valid values. k-Factor Defaults: Default k-factor values set 0.25 indicator group, unless overridden user-provided values k_factors. Reporting Completeness: Flags district-year reporting rates 75% imputes missing data using district-level medians account reporting inconsistencies. k-Factor Scaling: Adjusts service counts based k-factor reporting rate using following scaling formula: $$AdjustedValue = Value \times \left(1 + \left(\frac{1}{ReportingRate/100} - 1\right) \times k\right)$$ ReportingRate reporting rate percent, k k-factor indicator group. Outlier Detection: Identifies flags extreme outliers using Hampel's X84 method, marking values exceed 5 Median Absolute Deviations (MAD) median. Data Imputation: Replaces remaining missing values district-level medians ensure data completeness.

title: Calculate health coverage indicators — calculate_indicator_coverage
text: calculate_indicator_coverage computes key health coverage indicators across specified administrative levels (national, adminlevel_1, district). function integrates data multiple sources, including DHIS-2, UN estimates, ANC-1, Penta-1 survey data. calculates coverage rates variety vaccinations health metrics based projected, survey-derived, estimated denominators.

title: Calculate health coverage indicators — calculate_indicator_coverage
code: calculate_indicator_coverage(   .data,   admin_level = c("national", "adminlevel_1", "district"),   derivation_population = c("totbirths_dhis2", "totlivebirths_dhis2", "totunder1_dhis2",     "totpop_dhis2", "un_population", "un_births", "un_under1"),   un_estimates = NULL,   survey_estimates = NULL,   subnational_map = NULL,   anc1survey = .cd_method$denominators$anc1survey,   dpt1survey = .cd_method$denominators$dpt1survey,   survey_year = .cd_method$denominators$survey_year,   region = NULL,   show_district = TRUE,   sbr = .cd_method$denominators$sbr,   nmr = .cd_method$denominators$nmr,   pnmr = .cd_method$denominators$pnmr,   twin = .cd_method$denominators$twin,   preg_loss = .cd_method$denominators$preg_loss )

title: Calculate health coverage indicators — calculate_indicator_coverage
text: .data cd_data tibble containing DHIS-2, UN, ANC-1, Penta-1 data. dataset must include columns key population vaccination metrics. admin_level Character. Specifies administrative level calculations. Options include:"national", "adminlevel_1", "district". derivation_population Character. population column used base DTP1/ANC1-derived denominators (*derived columns). One "totbirths_dhis2", "totlivebirths_dhis2", "totunder1_dhis2", "totpop_dhis2", "un_population", "un_births" "un_under1". Defaults first. un_estimates Optional. tibble containing UN population estimates. Required national-level calculations. survey_estimates Optional. data frame subnational survey estimates (r_* columns r_anc1 r_penta1, optionally mortality rates). Used subnational levels replace default rates survey values available. Default NULL. subnational_map Optional. data frame mapping survey regions adminlevel_1 units, used joining survey_estimates. Default NULL. anc1survey Numeric. Survey-derived coverage rate ANC-1 (antenatal care, first visit). Default 0.98. dpt1survey Numeric. Survey-derived coverage rate Penta-1 (DPT1 vaccination). Default 0.97. survey_year Interger. year Penta-1 survey provided region Optional name adminlevel_1 region restrict calculation . valid admin_level = "adminlevel_1". Default NULL. show_district Logical. region supplied, whether return results district within region (TRUE, default) aggregated region. sbr Numeric. stillbirth rate. Default 0.02. nmr Numeric. Neonatal mortality rate. Default 0.025. pnmr Numeric. Post-neonatal mortality rate. Default 0.024. twin Numeric. Twin birth rate. Default 0.015. preg_loss Numeric. Pregnancy loss rate. Default 0.03.

text: Computes ratios specified pairs indicators dynamically flags whether calculated ratio falls within adequate range, per district year. function intermediate utility used standardize ratio calculations adequacy checks across indicator pairs.

title: Calculate indicator ratios and adequacy flags — calculate_ratios_and_adequacy

title: Calculate indicator ratios and adequacy flags — calculate_ratios_and_adequacy
text: .data data frame type cd_data. ratio_pairs named list indicator pairs ratios calculated. pair character vector length two, first element numerator second denominator. Default : list("ratioAP" = c("anc1", "penta1"), "ratioPP" = c("penta1", "penta3"), "ratioOO" = c("opv1", "opv3")). name list becomes name resulting ratio column. adequate_range numeric vector length two specifying inclusive lower upper bounds adequate range, typically 1 1.5. Ratios within range flagged adequate. region Optional. Restrict analysis one region (adminlevel_1).

title: Calculate indicator ratios and adequacy flags — calculate_ratios_and_adequacy
text: data frame columns : Summed indicators district year: Summed values indicator across districts within specified year, based input ratio_pairs. Ratios: ratio calculated sum specified numerator divided sum specified denominator pair. Adequacy flags: ratio, adequacy flag (e.g., adeq_ratioAP) generated, set 1 ratio falls within adequate_range, 0 otherwise. output aggregated year includes means ratios adequacy flags.

title: Calculate indicator ratios and adequacy flags — calculate_ratios_and_adequacy
text: function standardizes ratio calculations dynamically computing ratios adequacy flags specified pairs indicators. operates three main stages: Summing Indicators: Calculates sum indicator district year. Calculating Ratios: Divides summed numerator summed denominator pair ratio_pairs, creating column ratio. Checking Adequacy: Flags ratio adequate falls within specified adequate_range, returning 1 adequate 0 otherwise.

what: cd2030.core: Countdown to 2030 analysis of routine health facility data — cd2030.core-package
title: cd2030.core: Countdown to 2030 analysis of routine health facility data — cd2030.core-package
text: Loads country's routine facility data (Countdown Excel workbook, Stata .dta master file), checks quality, adjusts incomplete reporting outliers, chooses denominators, computes coverage, inequality, mortality, service utilization, health system family planning indicators, chart (plot()) result. Countdown apps – cd2030.rmncah, cd2030.vaxx cd2030.pooled – Shiny front ends , built pages, wizard app frame exports, datasuite.ui's interface kit report builder.

title: cd2030.core: Countdown to 2030 analysis of routine health facility data — cd2030.core-package
text: dataset: load_cache_data() opens workbook saved .rds CacheConnection, object holds one dataset every choice made (adjustments, denominators, surveys, mappings, chart options, saved reports) saves .rds next data file. load_data() gives just checked data; init_CacheConnection() makes object data .rds. Data quality: calculate_average_reporting_rate(), calculate_completeness_summary(), calculate_outliers_summary(), calculate_ratios_summary(), calculate_overall_score(); Load Data wizard's checks, run_all_quality_checks(). Adjustment: generate_adjustment_values(), adjust_service_data(). Denominators coverage: prepare_population_metrics(), calculate_indicator_coverage(), calculate_coverage(), calculate_inequality(). analyses: create_mortality_summary(), compute_service_utilization(), calculate_health_system_metrics(), generate_fpet_summary(), generate_bayes_model(). Reports: report_presets() (standard reports) export_report() (Word, PDF, PowerPoint). Indicator groups: list_indicator_groups(), set_selected_group(), register_indicator_group(). Apps: countdown-pages (cd_app() pages every Countdown app shares). README (https://github.com/damurka/cd2030.core) explains packages fit together, app built one, develop release .

title: Initialize or load a cached Countdown 2030 connection — load_cache_data
text: path Path .xlsx, .xls, .dta, .rds. indicator_group One "auto", "vaccine", "rmncah", "custom". Default "auto". profile Optional. Either name (string) existing group, definition register inline loading: explicit form: list(name = "rmncah", value = list(hiv = c("hiv_test","pmtct1"))) compact form:  list(hiv_profile = list(testing = c("hiv_test"), care = c("art_new"))) "custom", profile must resolve one concrete name. on_conflict Conflict policy profile definition: one "replace", "merge", "error". Default "replace". "merge" unions indicators per category. create_cache Logical. Excel/Stata inputs, whether pass path connection data path cache file created loaded next . Default FALSE (cache file). Ignored .rds inputs. start_year Optional integer filter minimum year. admin_sheet_name Excel sheet admin data. Default "Admin_data". population_sheet_name Excel sheet population data. Default "Population_data". reporting_sheet_name Excel sheet reporting completeness. Default "Reporting_completeness". service_sheet_names Character vector service-data sheets. Default: sheets matching "Service_data" supplied. validate Logical. Whether stop error merged data fails data quality check: check_district_consistency(), check_month_presence() check_month_validity(). Default TRUE. FALSE file problems still loads, caller can run checks later run_all_quality_checks(). Structural checks, missing Admin sheet column, always run.

title: cd2030.core 1.0.0
text: Initial Release CacheConnection now names file-backed cache source file’s basename (<stem>.rds) instead <country>_<timestamp>.rds, loads existing matching cache directly instead treating fresh parse authoritative one already present – decision now lives entirely CacheConnection , applies uniformly regardless caller. Added cd2030_mcp_server(), optional (mcptools/ellmer Suggests) Model Context Protocol server exposing read-tools – data quality, coverage, inequality, mortality, service utilization, health system, private-sector queries, plus report generation coverage charts – already-processed .rds cache, use LLM clients like Claude Desktop Claude Code. Expanded MCP server 12 38 tools, covering every remaining read-CacheConnection method (mutating setters non-data methods remain deliberately unreachable). Standardized MCP tool naming/documentation CD2030 analytical framework’s vocabulary (get_coverage_targets, get_continuum_of_care renamed match; DQA/mortality/health-system tool descriptions now cite framework’s official metric IDs named indices), added three “Equity Assessment” equiplot tools (get_equiplot_area, get_equiplot_wealth, get_equiplot_education), bringing total 41. Fixed stray print() debug statements generate_report(), generate_coverage_data(), generate_bayes_model() corrupted MCP server’s stdio JSON-RPC stream (stdout doubles wire protocol, incidental console output breaks every client response). MCP tool results now also capped total cell count (max_cells, default 5000), just row count: row-cap doesn’t protect wide table (e.g. get_indicator_coverage district level, ~190 columns), even handful rows produced megabyte-scale response crashed live client connection. Six MCP tools (get_overall_score, get_inequality, get_completeness_summary, get_outliers_summary, get_reporting_rate, get_service_utilization_summary) now read CacheConnection’s cached active bindings (e.g. reporting_rate_district) instead always calling always-recomputing calculate_*/compute_* method, whenever region filter requested – exact case bindings cover. Verified identical output direct recompute six.
